CarPlay can make any car feel more comfortable and inviting, but the stock experience isn't always perfect.

Some models still require a wired connection, while others don't support CarPlay at all, let alone charging and cooling your iPhone during long drives.

Fortunately, improving these areas doesn't require a big investment. The following affordable accessories cover everything from wireless CarPlay and MagSafe charging to cable management and adding a standalone display to older cars.

Going from wired to wireless CarPlay

If your vehicle already supports wired CarPlay, the Carlinkit Mini Ultra 3 lets you ditch the cable while retaining the car's touchscreen, steering wheel controls, built-in microphone, and factory audio system.

This compact adapter features both USB-A and USB-C ports. After the initial pairing, it automatically reconnects every time you start the car. It also supports wireless Android Auto on Android 11 or later, making it equally handy for vehicles shared between iPhone and Android users.

One important note — this adapter requires your vehicle to already have wired CarPlay; it cannot add CarPlay to vehicles that don't support it.

The Carlinkit Mini Ultra 3 is priced at $43.99, with Prime shipping.

Adding CarPlay to virtually any older car

For vehicles without CarPlay, buying a portable display is usually the simplest upgrade. The Krunia 9.26-inch portable CarPlay screen is $89.99 and adds wireless CarPlay without removing the factory head unit.

The display supports Bluetooth, AUX, and FM audio connections, as well as Siri, Android Auto, and OTA firmware updates. It also includes a reversing camera, but installing that part requires running cables to the rear of the car.

For those who want CarPlay without replacing the factory audio system, this is a rather attractive compromise.

Installing a permanent CarPlay head unit

A portable display won't suit every dashboard. For a tidier permanent installation, the BOSS Audio BVCP9700A is an affordable double-DIN head unit with a 7-inch touchscreen that supports Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, Bluetooth, and a reversing camera.

This head unit costs $164.99, but buyers should confirm compatibility with their car before ordering. Additional costs like a dash kit, wiring harness, steering wheel control adapter, or professional installation can push the overall price up.

Keeping your iPhone cool while charging

Wireless charging, navigation running, sunlight, and a hot dashboard can really put your iPhone through its paces. The ESR CryoBoost MagSafe car charger solves this with a built-in cooling fan. It combines a magnetic vent or dash mount, wireless charging, and active cooling. At $29.99, it's especially suited to drivers using wireless CarPlay who still want to charge their iPhone on long journeys.

When charging isn't necessary, a simpler MagSafe mount will do

Not every trip requires wireless charging. The standard ESR MagSafe mount holds your phone on the dashboard or air vent without extra charging cables.

Priced at $15.99, it comes with a metal ring sticker for phones or cases without built-in magnets. In hot climates, this may also be the better choice, since charging generates additional heat.

Replace unstable CarPlay cables

Many CarPlay issues ultimately come down to worn or poorly fitting cables. The Anker Nano USB-A to USB-C CarPlay cable features a braided design for more stable data transfer, works with newer iPhones using USB-C, and costs $11.99.

Drivers using an iPhone 14 or older can opt for Anker's PowerLine Flow USB-A to Lightning cable, priced at $17.99.

Add fast charging for the best experience

The USB port that powers wired CarPlay usually charges quite slowly. The Anker 323 car charger plugs into the 12V socket and provides one USB-C port and one USB-A port.

At $14.99, it's a budget-friendly way to charge a passenger's phone or power other accessories without interfering with the car's CarPlay connection, and it speeds up your own charging when using wireless CarPlay.

Tidy up your installation

A $6.99 pack of adhesive cable clips can make installing a portable CarPlay display or a wired phone holder look much neater. These clips route cables along the edges of the dashboard, keeping them away from the gear stick, pedals, and cup holders.

You don't need to change cars or go through an expensive audio system upgrade to use CarPlay. Depending on what your vehicle already supports, spending anywhere from $12 on a better cable to around $90 on a portable display can dramatically improve the daily experience.

Want to get even more out of CarPlay? Check out 9to5Mac's regularly updated list of over 120 iPhone apps that support CarPlay.
